question: Will Flávio Bolsonaro participate in TV Globo's first-round presidential debate on October 1, 2026?

calls.reasoning: Status quo is NO: both frontrunners skipped Band (Aug 23) and killed the Sept 14 consortium debate by not confirming; Flávio has an explicit, publicly restated condition (attends only if Lula does), and as of Now neither has confirmed for Globo. Reference class (Brazilian presidential frontrunners who boycotted earlier first-round debates, then faced the final pre-election Globo debate: Lula 2006 NO, Jair Bolsonaro 2018 NO, Lula/Bolsonaro 2022 YES but neither had been boycotting) implies roughly 1-in-4. Upward update: Lula's campaign blocked Sept 30 and Oct 1 of public commitments and reserved the eve for debate prep while trailing badly, a concrete option-preserving move reported Sept 21. Decomposing: P(Lula attends) ~0.45 x P(Flávio | Lula) ~0.85, plus ~0.04 for Flávio attending alone, x ~0.97 that the debate airs at all => ~0.39. Polymarket's broader 'any televised debate before Oct 3' contract at 42c (thin, $2.3k volume, includes the Sept 27 Record debate and virtual participation, so an upper bound on this one) pulls the Globo-specific number to roughly 0.36; PT's unresolved objection to the small-party invitees shades it slightly lower. Evidence is genuinely two-sided and the decisive fact (Lula's choice) is undetermined, so I stay near the reference class.

calls.reconciliation: Four disputes. (1) FACTUAL — whether Lula had already declined Globo: Run 3's VEJA ~Aug 26 'decided not to attend, already communicated' versus Runs 1–2's CNN Brasil Sept 21 'reevaluating, decision not closed, Sept 30–Oct 1 cleared, eve reserved for prep'. Settled by recency and specificity: the Sept 21 item is the newest reporting any run found and supersedes; the state is open, not declined. (2) FACTUAL, PARTLY UNSETTLEABLE — the unconditional Globo base rate: ~4/6 leaders present 2002–2022 (Runs 1–2, with Run 2 flagging its four attendances as unverified recall) versus roughly even 1989–2022 including Collor 1989 and FHC 1998 as absences (Run 3). No web access this run, so I cannot adjudicate the 1989/1998 cases and let that uncertainty stand; it is not load-bearing, because all three versions of the history agree the *conditional* class — prior-boycotter faces the final Globo debate — is 0-for-N, and that is the class I anchor on. (3) JUDGMENT, no tie-breaking evidence — is the cleared calendar a genuine tell (Run 1: P(Lula)≈0.45) or option-preservation (Runs 2–3: ≈0.38)? Clearing two days is costless and preserves both branches, and Lula's revealed 2026 behavior is two skips plus an isolation complaint the Globo invite list does not fix; I bet on ≈0.40, nearer Runs 2–3. (4) FACTUAL — the Polymarket contract's scope: all three read it identically and correctly as a superset (any televised debate through Oct 3, virtual participation counts, captures Record Sept 27) on thin volume, so it bounds rather than anchors this question; no dispute to settle. I retrieved nothing myself on this run, so 'sources' is empty by design. Final number is my own decomposition (0.95 × [0.40·0.82 + 0.60·0.05] ≈ 0.33), not an average; it lands inside the runs' range because the reconciled evidence puts it there.
